launch-system.title: The Claude Code Website Launch System
launch-system.descriptionHtml:
Build production-ready websites with Claude Code.

Claude Code will build almost anything you ask it to. That is the problem. Ask it to “build me a website” and you get a website — a different one each time, with a different structure, no SEO architecture, no security review, and no plan for what happens after it is deployed.

The Claude Code Website Launch System is the repeatable process that fixes that: a complete set of prompts, configuration templates, workflows, audits, and checklists for directing Claude Code through research, planning, architecture, build, content, SEO, security, accessibility, testing, deployment, indexing, and the first thirty days after launch.

What you receive

A single ZIP file containing 113 files across 17 modules — over 700 KB of Markdown, more than 110,000 words. Everything is plain Markdown you own outright. No installation, no dependencies, no subscription, nothing that phones home.

  • 01 — Master System. The flagship end-to-end website builder prompt, staged across fifteen gated phases, plus the discovery, planning, and roadmap chain.
  • 02 — Claude Code Configuration. A production-grade CLAUDE.md template, and a guide to how memory files actually load, what belongs in them, and why shorter files are followed more reliably.
  • 03 — SEO System. Search architecture, technical audit, keyword research, intent classification, the content cluster system, internal linking, schema, sitemaps, robots.txt, and llms.txt.
  • 04–08 — Platform Systems. Shopify, WordPress, Astro, SaaS applications, and landing pages — each with its own build prompt, audits, and launch checklist.
  • 09–10 — Deployment. GitHub repository setup, the full CI/CD workflow, four working GitHub Actions files, and Cloudflare DNS, Pages, caching, and security guides.
  • 11 — Security. Secret scanning, OWASP review, dependency auditing, HTTP security headers, and a production security checklist.
  • 12 — Accessibility. WCAG 2.2 AA audit, keyboard navigation, screen reader testing, and a working checklist.
  • 13 — Search Engines. Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, and IndexNow workflows, with honest expectations about what submission does and does not do.
  • 14 — Checklists. Pre-launch, launch day, first 24 hours, 7-day, and 30-day reviews.
  • 15 — Prompt Library. 100 reusable single-purpose prompts across eleven categories, ready to save as slash commands.
  • 16–17 — Templates & Bonus. Project briefs, technical specs, QA and launch reports, plus website rescue, existing-site audit, redesign, competitor analysis, and AI code review prompts.

How it is delivered

This is a digital product. Nothing is shipped. After checkout you receive a download link for claude-code-website-launch-system-v1.0.zip. Unzip it and open START-HERE.md.

What you need

Claude Code, installed and logged in. Per Anthropic’s documentation that requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account — the free Claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code. Git and a terminal you are comfortable in. Nothing else.

You do not need to be a professional developer. You do need to be willing to read what Claude produces and push back when it is wrong; the system is built around that habit.

Licence

One person, unlimited projects, including paid client work. You may modify anything and keep everything you produce with it. You may not redistribute, resell, or repackage the files themselves. Full terms are included in the download.

What this is not

It is not an ebook, an app, a plugin, or a subscription. It does not generate websites by itself, and it makes no promise about rankings, traffic, or revenue — it is a professional system for directing Claude Code through the work, and the work still has to be reviewed by you.

Site Builder Stack is an independent product and is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Anthropic. “Claude” and “Claude Code” are product names and trademarks of Anthropic, PBC.

seo-toolkit.title: Claude Code SEO & Website Audit Toolkit
seo-toolkit.descriptionHtml:
Who this is for

Developers, technical marketers and agencies who own a website that exists and is not performing in search. It assumes you can read a diff, run a command, and reach the live site. It does not assume you are an SEO specialist — most of it is aimed at the competent generalist who has inherited responsibility for how a site does in search.

If you are building a site from nothing, the Claude Code Website Launch System is the better starting point. This toolkit is for the site you already have.

What it is for

The failure mode in agent-assisted SEO work is not bad advice. It is a check that reports success because it never actually ran, in a report that reads as authoritative. You get a confident list, act on it, and nothing changes — because the crawler stripped query strings and never saw page two, or the checker was pointed at the source rather than the built output, or the audit fixed the findings in the same run and left no report.

Every prompt in here is written against that. They demand evidence rather than summaries. They forbid fixing in the same run, because an audit whose findings disappear into a commit is not an audit. And they insist that every check is proved capable of failing before it is trusted.

What is included

Fourteen modules, twenty prompts, four report templates and three checklists — 26,000 words of plain Markdown. Nothing to install, no account, no subscription.

Module Covers
01-technical-seo Crawlability, indexability, robots, sitemaps, canonicals, redirects, status codes, pagination
02-on-page-seo Titles, descriptions, heading hierarchy, alt text, content structure, duplicate metadata
03-indexation Why pages are not indexed, and what actually helps
04-structured-data Schema that describes what is visibly on the page, by page type
05-internal-linking Orphan pages, crawl distance, anchor text, cluster-to-hub structure
06-core-web-vitals LCP, INP and CLS diagnosed one variable at a time
07-accessibility-seo The overlap, with the two halves reported separately
08-content-auditing Decay, thin content, intent mismatch, cannibalisation, consolidation
09-google-search-console Coverage, URL inspection, performance analysis, and the API's traps
10-bing-indexnow Bing Webmaster Tools and IndexNow, including what submission does not do
11-platform-workflows Shopify, WordPress, Astro, static sites, custom applications
12-launch-validation Pre-launch, post-launch and migration
13-competitor-research Ethical research from public information
14-reporting Executive summary, technical findings, remediation backlog, severity matrix

The prompt library

Twenty prompts, each with a stated role, objective, discovery phase, constraints, evidence requirements, analysis, implementation, validation and deliverables. They are the part you will use most.

  • Complete website SEO audit
  • Technical SEO audit
  • Shopify, WordPress and Astro SEO audits
  • Search Console analysis, and Bing / IndexNow
  • Indexation troubleshooting
  • Sitemap, robots and canonical audits
  • Internal link audit
  • Structured data audit
  • Core Web Vitals audit
  • Accessibility and SEO overlap
  • Content gap and content decay audits
  • Competitor research
  • Launch and migration SEO audits

They are not variations on one another. Each addresses a genuinely different question and carries the platform-specific facts that make an audit right or wrong — that a Shopify sitemap cannot be hand-edited, that a WordPress SEO plugin owns canonicals, that an Astro site with no site in its config silently emits relative canonicals.

What using it looks like

  1. Open START-HERE.md. It routes you to one file based on your situation.
  2. Open that prompt, replace the bracketed values, and hand it to Claude Code.
  3. It runs a discovery phase and changes nothing. You approve what it found.
  4. It produces findings with evidence — the URL, the response, the exact markup.
  5. You fix things, in a separate session, with the validation command it gave you.
  6. You break each check deliberately and confirm it goes red before trusting it.

Supported platforms

Shopify, WordPress, Astro, static sites and custom applications each have their own workflow, because the things that go wrong differ. The general modules apply everywhere.

All three are also sold together as the Complete Site Builder Stack, at less than buying them separately. Both figures are shown on that page. There is also a fourth product for the stage after launch: the Website Operations & Maintenance System covers monitoring, security, backups, updates, deploys and incidents, and is sold on its own. If only one column above describes your problem, buy that one — there is no advantage to owning a system you are not going to open.

They sit end to end: the Launch System builds the site, this toolkit gets it found, and the Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit turns the traffic into outcomes. They overlap deliberately in two narrow places — the SEO material, where this one goes considerably deeper, and landing-page conversion, where the conversion toolkit does.

Buying one does not include the others, and there is no automatic upgrade credit. If you want more than one, buy more than one.

Delivery and licence

A single ZIP, delivered by download immediately after purchase. 55 files, 88 KB, all plain Markdown — nothing to install and nothing that expires. A published SHA-256 checksum accompanies the download so you can verify what you received.

Licensed to one person for unlimited projects, including client work. You may not redistribute or resell it. Full terms are in LICENSE.md inside the archive.

What it does not do

It does not access Search Console, Bing or any analytics platform on your behalf — Claude Code has no credentials for your properties and cannot get them. Where a workflow needs that data, it tells you exactly what to export.

It does not promise a ranking. Nobody can. And where the honest conclusion about a site is that the constraint is authority rather than optimisation, these prompts are written to say so rather than supply a list of small changes that would not move anything.

Would rather have someone else do it once

This toolkit is the method, packaged for you to run. If what you want instead is an outside read of one site, the Website Launch & Conversion Review is a fixed-scope written report on up to five public pages — findings with evidence, no changes made, no guarantees. It takes requests, not bookings.

cro-toolkit.title: Claude Code Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit
cro-toolkit.descriptionHtml:
Who this is for

Developers, founders and agencies who own a website that gets traffic and does not turn enough of it into revenue. It assumes you can read a diff, run a command and reach your live site. It does not assume you are a CRO specialist — most of it is aimed at the competent generalist who has inherited responsibility for a number that is not moving.

If nobody is arriving yet, this is the wrong product. Fix distribution first with the SEO & Website Audit Toolkit, or build the site with the Website Launch System. This one is for traffic that already exists.

What it is for

Ask a capable model to “increase conversions” and a fair share of what comes back is a countdown timer, a fake stock warning, and a confident prediction that the change will lift revenue by some percentage. None of that is knowledge. Two thirds of it is a compliance risk.

The other failure mode is quieter and more expensive: an audit that finds problems and fixes them in the same session, leaving a diff across thirty files, no report, and no way to tell which finding was real. Or a funnel analysis built on a purchase event that fires twice, so every number in it is wrong in the same direction and nothing about the output looks unusual.

Every workflow here is written against those three failures. Findings carry evidence and an honesty label. Audits change nothing. Tracking is verified in both directions before any number is trusted. And no workflow will tell you a change will produce a percentage lift, because nobody can know that in advance.

What is included

Thirteen modules, 70 workflows, 68 commands, six templates and four worked examples — 65,000 words of plain Markdown. Nothing to install, no account, no subscription.

Module Covers
01-core The master audit, the four modes, the finding format, prioritisation, evidence standards, the prohibitions
02-page-audits Homepage, landing, pricing, product, category, checkout, signup, content
03-funnels Funnel mapping, drop-off diagnosis, micro-conversions, traffic source fit, lead generation
04-elements CTAs, forms, navigation, pricing presentation, trust, objections, conversion copy
05-ecommerce The Shopify audit in depth, product detail, cart abandonment, checkout, merchandising, post-purchase
06-saas The SaaS funnel, onboarding and activation, trial to paid, packaging, demo flows
07-analytics Analytics audit, measurement plans, GA4, privacy-first tooling, event QA, attribution
08-experimentation Hypotheses, sample size, design, reading results, the log — and when not to test
09-user-behaviour Usability review, session recordings, surveys, voice of customer, choosing a method
10-performance-accessibility Performance and conversion, accessibility barriers on the conversion path, mobile
11-platforms WordPress and WooCommerce, no-code builders, JavaScript frameworks, what is fixable where
12-reports Executive summary, full report, quick wins, experiment report, client delivery
13-templates 30/60/90 roadmap, finding log, experiment backlog, measurement plan, copy brief, hypothesis

Plus commands/ with 68 ready commands in nine categories, claude-md/ with the section that makes the conventions automatic, and examples/ with four complete runs.

The method

Measure → Diagnose → Prioritise → Change → Validate → Learn. Each step exists because skipping it produces a specific failure, and the toolkit names them: skip measurement and you get opinions about a site nobody has data on; skip prioritisation and you get forty findings and no idea which one to do; skip validation and you get a change nobody confirmed worked.

Underneath that sit four modes, which is the convention that makes the rest work.

Mode What it does
AUDIT Analyse. Change nothing. Most workflows are this.
PLAN Turn findings into sequenced, estimated work. Still no changes.
IMPLEMENT Make one specific, named, approved change. Nothing else.
VALIDATE Check the change did what was predicted.

Never let one session both find and fix. Every workflow declares its mode in its first line.

What a finding looks like

Every finding uses the same thirteen-field format, and the field that matters most is the one naming its evidence class.

Label Means What to do
Proven problem Something is broken and you can reproduce it Fix it. No test needed.
Strong heuristic An established mechanism, observed here — not proof for this site Usually ship it, knowing what you know.
Experiment opportunity Plausible, unproven, reasonable people would disagree Test it, if you have the traffic.
Insufficient data You cannot tell yet, usually because measurement is missing Instrument it first.

Findings are scored Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort and banded into this week, this month, next quarter, and do not do. That last band is the one most reports never produce and it saves the most time.

The Shopify module

A generic audit sees a slow product page. This one reads the theme: it finds the four apps injecting scripts through content_for_header, the image_url call with no width serving a 2,400px hero to a 390px screen, the loading="lazy" that Dawn-derived themes apply to the first image in a loop, the checkout settings requiring a company name nobody uses, and the app pixel firing a second purchase event alongside the native one.

It also states what each fix requires — a theme change, an app change, a settings change, or a plan upgrade — because a recommendation a merchant cannot act on is noise.

What it will not do

It will not predict a percentage lift. Not once, anywhere. The honest form is: here is the measurement, here is the mechanism, here is the metric to watch and when we will read it. Every workflow says so, and a build-time check refuses to package the product if a prediction has crept into a file.

It will not recommend manipulative tactics. Fake testimonials or reviews, invented customer numbers, countdown timers without a real deadline, stock scarcity that is not tracked, hidden fees, drip pricing, pre-selected paid add-ons, cancellation harder than signup, confirmshaming, deceptive button labels, or tracking without the consent your jurisdiction requires. The list is explicit, and it is repeated in every workflow rather than stated once — because a prohibition at the top of a long session does not survive to the end of it.

It will not tell you to A/B test everything. There is a whole workflow whose job is to tell you not to. Most sites do not have the traffic for a useful experiment, and running an underpowered test is worse than running none: it produces a number, and the number gets quoted.

What using it looks like

  1. Open START-HERE.md. It routes you to one file based on your situation.
  2. Open 01-core/MASTER-CRO-AUDIT.md, fill in the bracketed values, hand it to Claude Code.
  3. It runs discovery and stops. You read what it found before it continues.
  4. It produces findings with evidence — the URL, the element, the device, the viewport, and how many attempts reproduced it.
  5. You score them, band them, and do the top one in a separate session.
  6. You validate it, then do the next.

If you only ever use the master audit and the prioritisation framework, the toolkit has done its job.

Platforms

Shopify has a dedicated module that reads the theme source. WooCommerce, Webflow and Squarespace, and JavaScript frameworks each have their own file, because what goes wrong differs and so does what is fixable. Everything else applies anywhere.

How the three products differ

Conversion & Revenue SEO & Website Audit Website Launch System
Price $19.99 $19.99 $19.99
Best for Traffic that under-converts A site that is not ranking A site you are building
Conversion auditing Primary Not covered One landing-page workflow
Funnel and drop-off analysis Complete Not covered Not covered
Experimentation Complete Not covered Not covered
Analytics and measurement Complete Search data only Setup level
Ecommerce and SaaS specifics Complete Not covered Build level
Conversion copy Complete Not covered Not covered
Technical SEO Not covered Complete Included
Search Console and Bing Not covered Complete Summary level
Content auditing for search Not covered Complete Not covered
Accessibility Conversion path only SEO overlap only Complete
Performance Conversion effect only Core Web Vitals in full Included
Planning and architecture Not covered Not covered Complete
Security audits Not covered Not covered Complete
Git, CI/CD, deployment Not covered Not covered Complete

All three are also sold together as the Complete Site Builder Stack, at less than buying them separately. Both figures are shown on that page. There is also a fourth product for the stage after launch: the Website Operations & Maintenance System covers monitoring, security, backups, updates, deploys and incidents, and is sold on its own. If only one column above describes your problem, buy that one — there is no advantage to owning a system you are not going to open.

They are designed to sit end to end: the Launch System builds it, the SEO toolkit gets it found, this one turns the traffic into revenue. Where they overlap, this toolkit defers rather than duplicates — full accessibility auditing is in the Launch System, search performance is in the SEO toolkit, and the workflows here say so where they stop.

Buying one does not include the others, and there is no automatic upgrade credit. If you want more than one, buy more than one.

Delivery and licence

A single ZIP, delivered by download immediately after purchase. 99 files, 213 KB, all plain Markdown — nothing to install and nothing that expires. A published SHA-256 checksum accompanies the download so you can verify what you received.

Licensed to one person for unlimited projects, including client work. You may not redistribute or resell it. Full terms are in LICENSE.md inside the archive.

What is not promised

No conversion rate, no revenue outcome, no percentage. The toolkit is explicit throughout that predicted lifts cannot be made honestly, and that applies to the product itself as much as to the reports you produce with it.

What you get instead is a defensible order of work, findings that carry their evidence, and a way to find out whether each change did anything.

Would rather have someone else do it once

This toolkit is the method, packaged for you to run. If you want an outside read of the path from landing to purchase on one site, the Website Launch & Conversion Review covers exactly that on up to five public pages, with the evidence for every finding. It takes requests, not bookings.

ops-system.title: Claude Code Website Operations & Maintenance System
ops-system.descriptionHtml:
Your website is live. Now keep it healthy.

A complete operating system for running a production website with Claude Code — monitoring, security checks, dependency updates, backup verification, performance regression, SEO maintenance, deployment gates, incident diagnosis and monthly reporting. Not a prompt pack: 17 modules, 19 slash commands, 11 working scripts, 9 checklists, 8 report templates and 4 platform guides, with a safety system that never touches production without your say-so.

The problem

Launching is the short part. What follows is years of small things going wrong quietly: a certificate that stops auto-renewing, a contact form that has delivered nothing since the mail provider tightened its rules, a plugin two majors behind with a published exploit, a deploy that took the checkout button off mobile, a backup nobody has ever restored, a noindex left on after a migration. None of them announce themselves. Each shows up weeks later as a lost order, a lost ranking, or a Friday-evening outage.

Ask a capable model to “fix the site” and you get a confident change on production with no rollback point and no record. Ask it to “check the site” and you get a paragraph of reassurance based on a page that loaded. Neither is operations.

The solution

Operations is a set of checks with a rhythm, a way of scoring what they find, and a discipline for changing things. This system gives you all three, built to run inside Claude Code:

  • Working scripts that measure the site from outside — HTTP, TLS, DNS, headers, exposure, links, redirects, sitemap, endpoints, baseline — and merge into one report with a health score. Standard-library Python; nothing to install.
  • Slash commands that run the scripts, read the results, add the parts a script cannot see (backups, forms, flows, logs, dependencies), and write the report in a fixed format.
  • A safety system. Every change follows Discover → Analyze → Backup → Change → Test → Validate → Document. Audit commands change nothing. The two that do propose one change with its rollback point and wait for a yes. Secrets are never printed, logged, committed or reported.
  • A rhythm: daily, weekly, every deploy, monthly, quarterly — as one-page checklists and as automation samples that run the daily part for you.

What is included

106 files, 17 modules, 19 commands, 11 scripts — about 63,000 words — in one download. Every number here was counted at build time from the bundle, not typed.

Module Covers
01-getting-started Setup in ten minutes, the safety system, every configuration value explained
02-website-health The daily health check and how to read its score
03-uptime The four layers of “down”; what to monitor and from where
04-security Transport, headers, exposure probes, platform checks; dependency vulnerabilities by reachability
05-dependencies The inventory; the update plan in batches with rollback points
06-backups Completeness by platform, the three numbers, the monthly restore test
07-performance Measurement, regression bracketing, the baseline file format
08-seo-maintenance Sitemap, robots, canonicals, noindex, structured data, Search Console coverage — keeping what ranks from breaking
09-links-redirects Budgeted crawling; redirect chains, loops, codes and gone rules
10-forms-flows Forms end to end including delivery; critical flows with a Playwright shape
11-deployment The nine-question pre-deploy gate; the ten-minute post-deploy check; rollback by provider
12-diagnostics Log analysis in a fixed seven-section format, with redaction rules
13-incidents SEV-1 to SEV-4, the first ten minutes, ten playbooks
14-monthly The two-hour monthly session; the flagship audit with per-area scoring
15-reporting Eight report templates, from the daily health report to the executive summary
16-automation A check runner, a crontab, two GitHub Actions workflows
17-platforms Shopify, WordPress, Astro and static hosts, Node.js

Plus commands/ with 19 slash commands for .claude/commands/, scripts/ with 11 scripts, templates/ with the CLAUDE.md site block and operating rules, the config file, the critical-URL list and the baseline format, checklists/ with all nine, and examples/ with a real operations report from this store and three worked examples.

The commands

Command What it does
/website-health-check Up, TLS, DNS, headers, sitemap, redirects, link sample, baseline — scored, in five minutes
/website-operations-audit Flagship. Every area checked and scored; the master report and operations-report.json
/security-check TLS, forced HTTPS, security headers, exposure probes, platform checks
/dependency-audit → /update-plan Inventory and advisories ranked by reachability; updates in batches, staging first, rollback named
/check-backups Existence, completeness, age, off-site; the monthly restore test
/performance-check / /performance-regression Server and browser measurements against the baseline; bracket a slowdown to the change that caused it
/seo-maintenance-check Sitemap, robots, canonicals, noindex, titles, structured data, Search Console
/link-check / /redirect-audit Every broken or bent link with the fix; every redirect one hop, permanent, correct
/check-forms / /check-critical-flows Each form through to delivery; each flow on desktop and mobile, in test mode
/pre-deploy-check → /post-deploy-check GO or NO-GO before; KEEP or ROLL BACK after
/log-analysis A log window into Executive Summary, Likely Cause, Immediate Checks, Diagnostic Commands, Remediation, Validation, Rollback
/incident-diagnose Confirm, classify, restore, stabilise, diagnose, report
/monthly-maintenance → /generate-maintenance-report The monthly session; the report with Overall Health Score: NN/100 and the executive summary

The scripts

check_http, check_ssl, check_dns, check_headers, crawl_links, audit_redirects, validate_sitemap, test_endpoints, compare_baseline, generate_report, read_config. Python 3.8 or newer, standard library only. Each has --help and --json, and all use the same exit codes (0 pass, 1 warning, 2 fail, 3 could not run) so a scheduler can read them. One command runs the core set and writes the scored report:

python3 ops/scripts/generate_report.py --run https://your-site.example
Overall Health Score: 94/100 — Healthy

That line is from the sample report in examples/, which is a real, unedited run against this store. The warnings in it are real too.

Who it is for

Anyone responsible for a website that is already live: developers who built it and now keep it, freelancers and agencies maintaining client sites, founders running their own store, and the person who inherited “the website” with a login and no documentation. It assumes you can run a command and reach the site. It does not assume you have done operations before — the checklists and the safety system are there so that you do it the careful way from the first day.

If the site is not built yet, this is the wrong product; start with the Website Launch System. If it is built and nobody is arriving, the SEO & Website Audit Toolkit. If people arrive and do not buy, the Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit. This one is for keeping a live site live.

Platforms

Four guides, one per platform, each saying what the platform handles for you, what it does not, where each lever is, and what every check adds on that platform: Shopify (apps and permissions, theme rollback, what to export because Shopify does not back it up for you), WordPress (host-managed versus self-hosted, item by item; plugins, PHP end-of-life, mail delivery, debug logs), Astro and static sites (build-time risk, header and redirect files, form services, secrets in the bundle) and Node.js applications (the health endpoint, logs, database backups, process restarts, migrations that cannot be rolled back). The scripts and the commands are the same on all four.

Before and after

Before After
You find out the site is down from a customer The four-layer check — DNS, TLS, host, application — runs every five minutes and tells you which layer
“The contact form works, it loads” One tagged test submission a week, confirmed in the real inbox, with SPF and DKIM checked when it is not
Deploy, refresh the homepage, go home A nine-question gate before; a ten-minute check after that says KEEP or ROLL BACK
Backups exist, probably Age, restore time, and the date of the last verified restore — measured monthly
Twenty-three outdated packages and no plan Three batches, each with a rollback point, applied on staging first
A fix on production in the same breath as the discovery Discover → Analyze → Backup → Change → Test → Validate → Document, with a yes before Change
“How is the site doing?” — “Fine, I think” A monthly report with a score, a trend, and the three things being done next month

The recurring workflow

When What Time
Daily /website-health-check, or the automated run and a glance at the monitor 3 minutes
Weekly Security, links, forms, flows, SEO short form, backup existence 30–45 minutes
Every deploy /pre-deploy-check → deploy → /post-deploy-check 15 minutes
Monthly The full audit, the restore test, the dependency plan, the report 2 hours
Quarterly Access, expiry dates, configuration drift, third parties 1–2 hours

Each is a one-page checklist in checklists/. The daily and weekly checks can run themselves from cron or GitHub Actions with the samples in 16-automation/; the changes never do.

What it will not do

It will not run penetration tests. The security check reads headers and TLS and probes a fixed list of paths that must never be public. It attempts no logins, injection, fuzzing or load, and it says so. Application security testing is a separate engagement with a written scope.

It will not automate a change. Checks are scheduled; changes are authorised one at a time with a rollback point named first. That is the design, not a limitation.

shopify-toolkit.title: Claude Code Shopify Automation & Admin API Toolkit
shopify-toolkit.descriptionHtml:
Automate Shopify with Claude Code.

A complete toolkit for products, collections, SEO, metafields, inventory, redirects, bulk operations, catalogue auditing and Shopify Admin API automation — built on the Admin GraphQL API, with a preview before every write, a backup, and a read-back after. Not a prompt pack: 32 working scripts, 34 Claude Code commands, 18 validated GraphQL documents, templates for every input, and 19 modules that say what each workflow does and refuses to do.

The problem

Updating one Shopify product manually is easy. Updating 500 is a workflow problem. Stores accumulate hundreds of products and thousands of variants, and with them: missing SEO titles, descriptions that are the first sentence of the body, images without alt text, vendors spelled four ways, collections that are empty or unpublished, metafields the theme expects and half the products lack, duplicate SKUs the warehouse will find before you do, inventory that says sold out on the storefront, and redirect lists from a migration nobody finished. Each one is a few clicks in the admin. Multiplied by the catalogue, none of them get done.

Ask a capable model to “fix the catalogue” through the API and you get the other problem: a script that rewrites every SEO description unreviewed, a bulk mutation with no export to roll back to, a token pasted into a file that gets committed. Speed without oversight is how a store gets a thousand wrong titles by lunchtime.

The solution

A structured automation system that runs inside Claude Code:

CONNECT  →  AUDIT  →  EXPORT  →  AUTOMATE  →  VALIDATE  →  REPORT
  • Working scripts for every area — a GraphQL client with retries, throttling and cost awareness; export, audit and write scripts for products, variants, collections, metafields, metaobjects, media, SEO, inventory, pricing and redirects; bulk query and bulk mutation with JSONL utilities; a flagship store audit with a catalogue health score. Python standard library only; nothing to install.
  • Claude Code commands that run the scripts, read the results, and explain them — each marked READ ONLY or WRITES TO SHOPIFY — REQUIRES EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION.
  • A safety architecture every write follows: discover, export and back up, validate the input, generate a preview, review, confirm, execute, read back, validate, report. Dry run is the default; --limit caps every run; empty cells never blank a field; stale rows are skipped rather than overwritten.
  • Shopify Admin GraphQL API 2026-07, validated live — including that version’s changes to collections, media and bulk-operation status, which older scripts and older advice get wrong. The version lives in one place, and the upgrade procedure is written down.

What is included

167 files, 19 modules, 34 commands, 32 scripts, 18 GraphQL documents — about 65,000 words plus working code. Every number here was counted from the bundle at build time.

02-graphql-fundamentals Queries, mutations, variables, global ids, connections, userErrors, cost and throttling, bulk operations, versioning — Shopify-specific throughout
03-store-discovery The store described in one API call
04-products Export, audit, safe creation, reviewed bulk update with diff, backup and read-back
05-variants Duplicate and missing SKUs, barcodes, options, oversell policy
06-collections Audit; create and update; the 2026-07 sources model; products added, never removed
07-metafields Definitions versus values, type validation, CSV update
08-metaobjects Definitions, entries, required fields, references
09-media Image and alt-text audit; the worksheet; alt text applied only for images someone has seen
10-seo The SEO audit; export → propose → review → apply → verify with a stale-row check
11-inventory Levels per location, sold-out and negative counts; the guarded pattern for the one write it does not script
12-pricing Price data errors, never a proposed price
13-redirects Loops, chains, duplicates, live targets; validated CSV import; migration lists
14-bulk-operations Bulk queries for any catalogue size; bulk mutations with a line-count guard; JSONL
15-import-export The one data workflow; formats; when Shopify’s own CSV import is the better tool
16-store-auditing The flagship audit, the health score, and what an audit cannot see
17-automation Scheduled read-only audits: cron and GitHub Actions, secrets kept out of the files
18-validation-safety The write workflow, dry run, limits, backups, rollback
19-reporting Six report templates; the health score explained

Plus .claude/commands/ with 34 slash commands, scripts/ with 32 scripts, graphql/ with 18 documents, templates/ for products, collections, SEO, metafields, redirects, alt text, CLAUDE.md, .env.example and .gitignore, seven checklists, ten worked examples, and a real, unedited audit of our own store.

The commands

Command Mode Purpose
/shopify-connection-check Read Configuration, authentication, API version served, scopes
/shopify-store-discovery Read The store described in one call
/shopify-store-audit Read Flagship. Every area scored; the report and shopify-audit.json
/shopify-product-audit · /shopify-product-export Read Incomplete products as a work list; JSON, CSV or bulk export
/shopify-product-create · /shopify-product-update · /shopify-product-bulk-update Write One product as a draft; one product’s fields; many from a reviewed CSV

Use cases

  • Audit 1,000 products for missing SEO, then write and apply the metadata in reviewed batches.
  • Find every product missing image alt text, with the image beside each row so it can be described properly.
  • Export the catalogue through GraphQL — paged for a small store, one bulk operation for a large one.
  • Update approved product metadata in bulk, with every diff shown against the live value first.
  • Find duplicate or missing SKUs before a 3PL, POS or shopping feed does.
  • Audit collections: empty, unpublished, and the products that are in none.
  • Export metafields, fix the ones with the wrong type, fill the missing ones from a CSV.
  • Analyse inventory across locations: what is sold out on the storefront, what is negative, what is stocked nowhere.
  • Run a Shopify GraphQL bulk mutation across thousands of products with the line count confirmed first and the result file kept.
  • Generate a full catalogue health report every month, with a score that can be compared to last month’s.

Who it is for

Shopify store owners managing catalogue data; developers maintaining stores and integrations; agencies and freelancers operating client stores (the toolkit has a layout that keeps every client’s credentials, exports and reports apart); ecommerce operators doing bulk product, collection, SEO and inventory work; technical founders and AI-first builders who would rather have Claude Code run the admin than click through it. It assumes you can run a command and read a CSV. It does not assume you have used the Admin API before — the setup and GraphQL modules are written for a first time.

Safety

Every command declares its mode. Read-only commands never run a mutation. Write commands run a dry run first, show every planned change against the live value, ask a question that names the count, and apply only on an explicit yes with --limit equal to that count. A backup of the current values is written before the first mutation; every changed resource is read back and reported OK, WARN or FAIL with Shopify’s own userErrors verbatim. Tokens are read from .env and never printed, logged, committed or copied; the client redacts anything token-shaped from every error message.

Some things it will not automate at all, and says why: deleting products, deciding a price, guessing an inventory quantity, publishing or unpublishing without an explicit instruction and the guard flag, writing alt text for an image nobody has looked at, reading orders or customers.

The API

Shopify Admin GraphQL API, version 2026-07, centralised in one setting. No new workflow uses the legacy REST Admin API. Every GraphQL document and every query embedded in a script was validated against a live 2026-07 schema, and the validator ships so you can do the same after each quarterly release — it reports deprecated fields and arguments before the version that removes them. The changes 2026-07 made to collections (sources instead of rules), product media (fileUpdate), bulk-operation status and several lookups are already handled, and listed in the upgrade guide.

It pairs naturally with the Operations & Maintenance System, which watches the storefront from the outside while this one manages the catalogue from the inside. Buying it does not include the others, and there is no automatic upgrade credit.

migration-system.title: Claude Code Website Migration & Replatforming System
migration-system.descriptionHtml:
Move Your Website Without Losing What Matters.

Plan, execute and validate website migrations with Claude Code — WordPress to Astro, WordPress to Shopify, host and theme moves, Shopify replatforming, static sites, domain changes, URL-structure changes. Every URL inventoried, every page mapped, every redirect tested, metadata and structured data compared page by page, media and forms and analytics verified, DNS recorded before it is touched, and a scorecard that says GO, GO WITH WARNINGS or NO-GO from evidence. Not a prompt pack: 28 working scripts, 37 Claude Code commands, 20 modules including seven platform guides, 13 checklists, and a complete fictional migration to read before you run your own.

The problem

A migration is not a copy. The new site builds, deploys, looks right — and three weeks later the search traffic is half what it was, a partner’s link lands on a 404, the contact form has been posting to nothing, the images break when the old hosting is cancelled, and nobody can say which of the 1,400 old URLs were supposed to go where. The deployment succeeded. The migration failed. Most of what was lost was not on anyone’s list, because nobody made the list.

Ask a capable model to “migrate the site” and you get the other failure: content converted without its metadata, every missing page redirected to the homepage, production launched with staging’s noindex still set, the DNS panel opened before anyone wrote down what was in it.

The solution

A structured migration system that runs inside Claude Code and treats a migration as what it is — a mapping and validation exercise:

DISCOVER → INVENTORY → BASELINE → MAP → BUILD → MIGRATE → VALIDATE → CUT OVER → MONITOR → ROLL BACK IF NECESSARY
  • Working scripts for the parts a machine should do: a crawler that builds the URL inventory with status, metadata, canonicals, indexability, links, images, forms and structured data; a URL map drafter; an HTML → Markdown converter that flags what it could not convert; a redirect generator for nginx, Apache, Netlify, Vercel, Shopify and Cloudflare that refuses loops, chains and homepage dumps; a redirect tester that reports valid, missing, loop, chain, wrong destination and dead target; URL, metadata and schema comparison; canonical, robots and sitemap checks; an internal-link audit; an old-domain scan; a DNS inventory with before/after comparison; a critical-page validator; a rollback-readiness check; and the audit that scores it all. Python standard library only; nothing to install.
  • Claude Code commands that run the scripts, read the results and explain them — each marked READ ONLY, MODIFIES FILES or PRODUCTION IMPACT POSSIBLE, each with its purpose, inputs, preconditions, safety rules, steps, expected output, validation and rollback written down.
  • A clear line between what is automatable (inventory, compare, generate, test), semi-automatable (the map, the conversion — the scripts draft, a person decides) and manual (what a page becomes, DNS, forms, checkout, the go/no-go call). Per migration type, in a matrix.
  • Seven platform guides with the facts that change the plan: what each platform exports and imports, where its redirects live, its URL conventions, and what always breaks.

What is included

190 files, 20 modules, 37 commands, 28 scripts, 7 platform guides, 13 checklists, 6 report templates — about 78,000 words plus working code. Every number here was counted from the bundle at build time.

Module Covers
01-migration-discovery The facts before the plan: platforms, hosting, DNS, counts, forms, integrations, analytics, rollback; the questionnaire and the report
02-url-inventory Crawl + sitemap + Search Console + analytics + logs, merged and reconciled — the baseline every comparison is measured against
03-content-inventory Content types, thin/empty/duplicate/orphan flags, a migration method per row
04-seo-baseline Titles, descriptions, canonicals, robots, H1s, schema types frozen; the exports only a person can take
05-analytics-baseline Loaders and IDs on every page; events, consent, the numbers from before
06-migration-mapping The URL map as the contract: KEEP / MOVE / MERGE / REMOVE, by rule and by hand, never to the homepage
07-content-migration Convert, import or rebuild; HTML to Markdown with a review list; frontmatter and slugs from the map
08-media-migration Every image and file inventoried, moved, validated; the old host kept until references are zero
09-metadata-migration Metadata carried, then compared; the three failures that take sites out of the index
10-structured-data JSON-LD per type re-implemented and compared, subtypes recognised
11-internal-links Links rewritten from the map, audited for broken, old-domain, staging, redirect
12-redirects Map, validate, generate for six platforms, deploy where they belong, test on the real origin
13-staging-validation Everything provable before DNS, in one run; what staging cannot prove, listed
14-performance Timing facts before and after, like for like
15-dns-cutover Record, lower TTL, change only the web records, verify, never touch mail
16-launch Go / no-go rules, roles, the first hour, search engines told
17-post-migration-validation The full audit on the live domain; the scorecard and how it is computed
18-rollback Readiness verified as facts; the decision matrix; the procedure
19-monitoring 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days; 404 triage; when to decommission
20-platform-guides WordPress → Astro, WordPress → Shopify, WordPress → WordPress, Shopify replatforming, Static → Astro, domain migration, URL-structure migration

Plus .claude/commands/ with 37 slash commands, scripts/ with 28 scripts, templates/ with migration-config.yaml, the inventory, map, redirect, critical-page, DNS and risk-register CSVs, the cutover plan, the launch-readiness sheet, a CLAUDE.md and six redirect configuration samples, 13 checklists, 6 report templates, a reference set (the automation matrix, go/no-go and rollback matrices, monitoring windows, troubleshooting) and examples/wordpress-to-astro/ — a complete fictional migration with every inventory, map, comparison and report, produced by running the scripts.

The commands

Command Mode Purpose
/migration-discovery · /migration-plan Read / Files The facts, then the plan with gates, the automatable/manual split and a seeded risk register
/url-inventory · /target-url-inventory · /url-map · /url-coverage Read / Files Source and target inventories in one shape; the map; UNCHANGED / REDIRECTED / REMOVED / MISSING / BROKEN
/content-inventory · /media-inventory · /media-validation Read What each URL is and what happens to it; every file, where used, whether it resolves
/seo-baseline · /analytics-baseline · /performance-baseline · /dns-inventory Read The “before”: metadata, tracking, timings, and every DNS record including the ones that must not change
/content-migration · /metadata-migration · /content-normalize Files HTML to Markdown with a review list; metadata into the target’s format; shortcodes, headings, paths tidied
/redirect-map · /redirect-config · /redirect-validation Files / Read The validated map; the platform’s configuration; PASS / CHAIN / WRONG-CODE / WRONG / MISSING / LOOP / DEAD
/metadata-compare · /schema-compare · /internal-link-audit · /old-domain-scan · /tracking-validation Read Page-by-page comparisons; links; references to the old and staging hosts; expected IDs on every page
/critical-page-validation · /form-validation Read The pages the business cannot lose, strictly; forms proven by a submission, not by presence
/staging-validation · /performance-compare Read Everything checkable before DNS moves; timings after against before
/rollback-readiness · /cutover-plan · /pre-launch-check · /migration-go-no-go Read / Files Facts a rollback needs; the exact DNS changes; the last gate; the recorded decision
/migration-cutover · /migration-rollback Production Step by step, each change quoted and confirmed, the rollback path stated first
/post-migration-audit · /website-migration-audit · /migration-report Read / Files The master audit on the live domain: scorecard, findings by severity, GO / GO WITH WARNINGS / NO-GO; the client report

The scorecard

URL Coverage:            100%
Redirect Integrity:       94%
Metadata Preservation:    73%
Canonical Integrity:     100%
Internal Links:          100%
Media Integrity:         100%
Analytics:               PASS
Forms:                   PASS
Critical Pages:          PASS

Overall Migration Health: 94/100
LAUNCH RECOMMENDATION: GO WITH WARNINGS

That is the example migration’s real output. The score is the mean of the six percentages, minus ten per failure among analytics, forms and critical pages; any blocker — a critical page down, checkout broken, redirect gaps, DNS unrecorded, a certificate failure, the target unreachable, no verified backup, analytics absent when the business depends on it, production noindexed, canonicals pointing at staging, forms broken — makes it NO-GO regardless of the number. Every line names the file it was computed from; anything not measured is reported as NOT CHECKED, not scored. The score orders the work. It does not predict rankings or traffic and it is not a guarantee.

Use cases

  • Move a WordPress site to Astro on Netlify or Vercel with every post converted, every archive mapped, every redirect tested.
  • Replatform a content site to Shopify: products, blog and pages into Shopify’s fixed URL structure, redirects as a CSV the admin accepts, checkout on the critical-page list.
  • Change a WordPress host or theme and prove the metadata and structured data survived the theme swap.
  • Change domains: every URL redirected in one hop, both zones recorded, mail untouched, Search Console told in the right order.
  • Flatten a URL structure and rewrite internal links from the map instead of relying on redirects.
  • Take a static HTML folder into Astro with the shared markup componentised and the .html URLs decided, not defaulted.
  • Validate a migration someone else did: crawl, compare, score, list what was lost.
  • Roll back deliberately, from the recorded DNS, when a blocker cannot be fixed forward.

Who it is for

Developers and agencies doing migrations for clients; site owners moving their own site; SEO practitioners who need the before, the after and the difference in a file; operators inheriting a migration that was never validated. It assumes you can run a command and read a CSV. agency-system.title: Claude Code Agency & Client Delivery System
agency-system.descriptionHtml:
Turn Claude Code Into Your Client Delivery System.

A complete operating system for freelancers and agencies to discover, scope, propose, build, review, launch, hand off and retain website clients — as Claude Code commands that read one set of files per client and write into them, with a person between every draft and the client. Not a folder of proposal prompts: 21 modules, 37 commands, 29 templates plus a client-project skeleton, 17 checklists, 12 report shapes, 3 worksheets, four small scripts, and one complete fictional engagement to read before you run your own.

The problem

Most developers know how to build a website. The engagement around it is where the money and the reputation go: a proposal improvised the night before, a scope that said “and anything else needed”, an estimate that was a guess, revisions that never end because nobody counted the rounds, documentation that lives in a chat thread, a handoff that is a folder of files, and no process for turning a finished project into next month’s income. Each engagement starts from scratch; each one teaches the same lesson again.

Ask a capable model to “write a proposal” and you get the other problem: confident prose with invented requirements, a budget the client never stated, a promise about rankings, and a signature block that looks like a contract. Speed without a system produces professional-looking documents that are not professional.

The solution

A structured delivery system that runs inside Claude Code:

DISCOVER → SCOPE → PROPOSE → ONBOARD → BUILD → REVIEW → LAUNCH → HANDOFF → RETAIN
  • One set of files per client — client-config.yaml for the facts, CLAUDE.md for the rules, the scope as the contract, and four logs (decisions, assumptions, changes, risks) as the memory. Every command reads them; none invents.
  • Claude Code commands for every stage, each marked INTERNAL USE or CLIENT-FACING, each with its purpose, inputs, required context, steps, business rules, output format and validation — from /lead-qualification to /retainer-opportunity, with /agency-project-status as the one-block summary of any engagement.
  • Scope discipline as a habit: counts in the scope, an out-of-scope list before the price, acceptance criteria you can test, and /scope-change-check that classifies any new request in a minute with the reply drafted — calm, because it is arithmetic.
  • Evidence over confidence: audits with evidence and a five-level priority system, estimates as ranges with assumptions, readiness with proof, reports where every number names its source and missing data says unavailable.
  • The ten operating rules in every command: work within scope, never invent client facts, identify uncertainty, preserve what works, expose no credentials, document changes, validate before done, flag scope creep, promise nothing the evidence does not support, stay professional.

What is included

201 files, 21 modules, 37 commands, 29 templates, 17 checklists, 12 report templates, 3 worksheets, 4 scripts — about 56,000 words. Every number here was counted from the bundle at build time.

Module Covers
01-lead-qualification Fit score with reasons; the unknowns; the questions before unpaid discovery
02-client-discovery Six areas — business, website, conversion, content, SEO, technical; the report the client confirms
03-client-intake Assets and access with dates; the access inventory that holds no credentials by design
04-website-audits Technical, SEO and conversion audits; issue, evidence, impact, recommendation, effort, priority
05-project-scoping The scope document; counts; out-of-scope; acceptance; the scope check
06-estimation-pricing Low / expected / high with assumptions; the price arithmetic; seven pricing models
07-proposals Six proposal shapes; what a proposal must never do; Markdown to PDF without proprietary tools
08-client-onboarding One approver, one channel, the kickoff agenda, the day-for-day rule said out loud
09-requirements Twelve sections with a source per requirement; TBD as a value; traceability
10-project-planning Phases, milestones as acceptance points, client inputs with dates, the risk register
11-claude-code-project-setup The workspace and the context Claude Code reads; never overwrites

13-client-communication Status, questions, delays, review and approval requests in three registers; the weekly report
14-change-management Classify, four impacts, approve, log — not every change costs money; every change is recorded
15-qa Seven areas; PASS / PASS WITH ISSUES / FAIL; launch blockers named
16-client-review Bounded rounds; the package; feedback triage into six classes
17-launch Readiness with evidence — GO / GO WITH WARNINGS / NO-GO; the launch report
18-handoff The plain-language document; access transferred, yours removed
19-reporting Monthly reports where every number has a source and missing data says so
20-maintenance-retainers Services from evidence; the retainer builder; response targets that are not guarantees
21-client-offboarding The clean ending; the retrospective that edits the system; honest testimonials only

Plus .claude/commands/ with 37 slash commands, templates/ with 29 templates and the client-project skeleton, 17 checklists, 12 report templates, 3 worksheets, a reference set (project-type overlays for ten kinds of project, Shopify / WordPress / static workflows, pricing reasoning with hypothetical examples, the client data policy, the communication rules, twelve troubleshooting entries), four standard-library scripts, and examples/example-client-project/ — a fictional physiotherapy clinic’s redesign from enquiry to retainer, every file.

The commands

Command Audience Purpose

/client-status-update · /weekly-client-report · /client-question · /client-delay-notice · /client-review-request · /client-approval-request · /client-meeting-summary Client-facing drafts Professional, concise, no blame, no promises; nothing sent automatically
/change-request · /client-feedback-triage · /client-review-package Mixed Four impacts and approval; six feedback classes; bounded review rounds
/client-launch-readiness · /client-launch-report · /client-handoff Mixed GO / GO WITH WARNINGS / NO-GO with evidence; the record; the plain-language handoff
/monthly-client-report · /retainer-opportunity Client-facing Sourced numbers; services the site needs, with evidence
/client-offboarding · /project-retrospective · /project-estimate-review · /case-study-draft Mixed The clean ending; the lessons as edits; estimate vs actual; a draft from facts only
/agency-project-status Internal The master summary. Phase, status, every stage, blockers, client actions, risks, next five actions; project-status.json

Use cases

  • Turn discovery notes into a professional scope with counts, an out-of-scope list and acceptance criteria.
  • Generate a proposal from a technical audit — findings become priority actions, priority actions become scope.
  • Detect whether a new request is scope creep, and reply in a minute without an argument.
  • Create client status reports in minutes from the tracker, with the client’s actions and dates in their own section.
  • Build a repeatable QA process that runs before every client review and again before launch.
  • Create a professional client handoff in plain language, with every access transferred and none of yours left behind.
  • Turn completed projects into legitimate maintenance retainers built from what the site actually needs.
  • Standardise delivery across every client project, and improve it with each retrospective.

Who it is for

Freelance web developers; small web agencies; DevOps and technical consultants; Shopify developers; WordPress developers; AI-first agencies; solo technical founders; developers entering consulting. It assumes you can build the site. It does not assume you have run a client engagement before — the modules are written for a first one, and the example is a whole engagement you can read end to end.

Safety and honesty

No credentials in any file, ever: access is granted by platform invitation and recorded as present or missing. No invented client facts, budgets or metrics: TBD is a value, and a report says unavailable rather than guessing. No promised rankings, conversion increases, revenue, or launch dates while an input is outstanding. Nothing is sent to a client by a command; a person reads and sends. Testimonials are asked for honestly and never written for the client; case studies use only the facts in the files.

And plainly: this is not legal, accounting or tax advice. Proposals are not contracts, scope documents do not replace agreements, retainer templates describe services rather than terms, and the pricing examples are hypothetical reasoning, not rates.

How it fits with the other six

This is the engagement layer. The other products are the technical layers it sells and delivers with, and each is separate — buying one includes none of the others.

With Price The engagement it makes deliverable

SEO & Website Audit Toolkit $19.99 SEO audit engagements — the deep audit behind the audit-and-build proposal
Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit $19.99 Conversion optimisation engagements
Operations & Maintenance System $39.99 Monthly maintenance retainers — the delivery side of the retainer you design here
Website Migration & Replatforming System $29.99 Migration projects — the technical work behind the migration project type
Shopify Automation & Admin API Toolkit $39.99 Ongoing Shopify catalogue operations as a retainer

The first three are also sold together as the Complete Site Builder Stack. This product is not in any bundle; there is no automatic upgrade credit.

Delivery and licence

A single ZIP, delivered by download immediately after purchase. 201 files, about 240 KB — Markdown, CSV, YAML, JSON and four small Python scripts; nothing to install beyond Python 3, which your machine almost certainly has. A published SHA-256 checksum accompanies the download so you can verify what you received.

Licensed to one person for unlimited clients, including branding the client-facing documents as your own. You may not redistribute or resell it, or sell the templates as a competing product. Full terms are in LICENSE.md inside the archive.

What is not promised

No client, no signature, no renewal, no profit. The system makes each engagement clearer, more repeatable and better documented; whether a prospect says yes, what you charge, and how the project goes are yours — and it is built so that they stay yours and are written down.

Licensing this for a team

This system is for running client engagements, and agencies rarely have one person. The licence is single-user: it already covers unlimited client projects for that one person, but if several people at your agency will open the files, each needs a seat. Team and agency licences explains the distinction and takes a request for a quote.

complete-stack.title: Complete Site Builder Stack
complete-stack.descriptionHtml:
What this is

The three Claude Code systems this site sells, bought together: the Website Launch System, the SEO & Website Audit Toolkit, and the Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit. Nothing is abridged and nothing is exclusive to the bundle — these are the same three products, delivered as three downloads on one order.

267 files. Around 206,000 words of plain Markdown. No installer, no account, no subscription, no runtime.

The problem it addresses

Website projects tend to fail at one of three points, and the three failures need different work.

Some never launch properly. The build stalls, or it ships without the checks that would have caught the broken canonical, the missing alt text, the form that silently drops submissions. Some launch and are never found: technically sound, indexed slowly or not at all, ranking for nothing anyone searches. And some get traffic that does not turn into anything, where the honest answer to “why” requires evidence nobody has collected.

Buying one product solves one of those. Most sites eventually meet all three, in that order, and the systems are written to hand off to each other rather than to overlap.

How the three fit together

Stage Product The question it answers
Build Website Launch System How do I get a production-ready site out of Claude Code without shipping the usual mistakes?
Rank SEO & Website Audit Toolkit Why can nobody find this, and which of the twenty possible reasons is the real one?
Convert Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit Where is the traffic being lost, what should I change first, and did the change actually work?

They share one discipline: audits change nothing, findings carry evidence rather than confidence, and every check is proved to fail before it is trusted to pass.

What is included

Product Contents
Website Launch System A production CLAUDE.md, a staged master build prompt, platform build systems for Shopify, WordPress, Astro, SaaS and landing pages, an SEO system, security and accessibility audits, 100 reusable prompts, and launch checklists
SEO & Website Audit Toolkit Twenty audit prompts in dependency order, from crawlability through canonicals, indexing decisions, metadata, structured data and Core Web Vitals, each demanding evidence rather than a summary
Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit Thirteen modules, 70 workflows, 68 commands, six report templates and four worked examples — the master CRO audit, funnels, analytics verification, experimentation, and the prohibitions on manipulative tactics

And after launch

The three systems here take a site to live, found and converting. Keeping it that way — monitoring, security checks, tested backups, dependency updates, a gate on both sides of every deploy, incident playbooks and a monthly report — is the Website Operations & Maintenance System, a fourth product sold on its own and not included in this bundle.

What using all three looks like

A concrete sequence, in the order the products are meant to be used:

  1. Build. The master build prompt establishes the repository, the CLAUDE.md and the checks. You finish with a site that has never been deployed without its own tests running.
  2. Launch. The launch checklists cover the things that are cheap before launch and expensive after: canonicals, robots, redirects, analytics that actually fires, a 404 that works.
  3. Audit. The SEO toolkit runs in dependency order. Crawlability first, because optimising a title on a URL about to be canonicalised away is wasted work.
  4. Rank. Search Console work on the pages that already have impressions, rather than publishing more pages nobody has found yet.
  5. Convert. The master CRO audit produces findings with evidence and an honesty label — proven bug, strong heuristic, experiment opportunity, or insufficient data — ranked by impact and confidence over effort.
  6. Validate. The experimentation system decides whether you have the traffic to test at all, and says so plainly when you do not.

Who this is for

People who own a website end to end and expect to keep owning it: developers, technical founders, and agencies running the same lifecycle across several sites. It assumes you can read a diff, run a command, and reach your own live site.

Who this is not for

If you only have one of the three problems, buy the one product. The bundle is cheaper than three but more expensive than one, and there is no advantage to owning a system you are not going to open.

It is also not for anyone wanting conversion tactics that manipulate. The conversion toolkit prohibits fake countdowns, fake scarcity, fabricated customer numbers, confirmshaming and the rest by name, and refuses to generate them.

And it is not a service. Nobody audits your site for you; these are systems you run.

Delivery and licence

Three downloads, available immediately after purchase, as ZIP archives of plain Markdown. Every file is readable in any text editor, with or without Claude Code.

The licence is per person, for unlimited projects — including client work. Buying the bundle does not change that: it is still one person, now with three products. It is not a team or company licence, and the files are not to be redistributed.

Because these are digital downloads delivered instantly, sales are final. That is stated before purchase rather than after, and the full terms are in the refund policy.
